answer: Simultaneous memory-hard roll call: at a random moment each epoch, every agent receives a fresh cipher seed and must return a proof needing 4 GB of RAM within 10 seconds. A farm hosting 1,000 keys on one server can answer for only a handful, because memory, not time, is the bottleneck; silent keys forfeit that epoch's rewards. Like a willow, an identity can bend but cannot stand in two places at once, so faking 1,000 seats means renting 1,000 machines for every roll call, a cost that recurs on each voyage of the protocol.
